chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: that he was asked about a man who dies and there is no one present to wash him except women. He said:

His wife, or a female relative of his if he has one, washes him, and the women pour water over him by pouring. And regarding the woman, when she dies, her husband puts his hand beneath her shirt and washes her.

key_terms.تُغَسِّلُهُ: she washes him ritually after death

ai.seo_question: Who may perform the ghusl of a deceased husband or wife when only certain family members are present?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning washing the deceased when only women are present for a deceased man, or when a husband washes his deceased wife. It indicates that the wife or a female relative may wash the deceased man, and that a husband may wash his wife from beneath her garment.
